findings.claim: DT changes the supplied advantages and returns. The actor still calls the original PPO policy-loss owner, combines the original entropy and KL losses, performs the original microbatch backward and gradient clip, and reaches the original AdamW owner. This audit introduces no substitute objective or normalization.
limits: Source identity does not prove the quality of the measured DT advantages or all historical model gradients.
Recorded configuration values below belong to saved diagnostic receipts; startup batch size must not be mistaken for the normalized per-worker batch size.

findings.evidence_status: source mechanism; degradation attribution remains conditional
findings.claim: The original ratio is exp(log_prob-old_log_prob), and the clipped/dual-clipped surrogate still multiplies the provided advantages. Clipping does not estimate or correct their sign or bias. It is a surrogate branch, not a hard bound on all parameter changes or a guarantee of improved task quality.
findings.conditional_explanation: If a persistent erroneous task direction existed, finite successive updates could accumulate a smooth loss of ability without requiring exploding advantages or NaN. The source supports this possibility, not its occurrence in this run.
not_proven: Actual systematic bias of DT advantages.
That a printed clipping fraction of zero implies small, harmless or correct parameter updates.

findings.claim: Official GRPO first sums each saved row token_level_rewards. It groups scores by the supplied index/UID (and optionally de-duplicates index/traj_index pairs), then subtracts the group mean and, when enabled, divides by group std plus 1e-6. A one-member group uses mean=0,std=1. The recorded native diagnostic uses eight environment rollouts per prompt; its startup worker rollout.n is one.
limits: Eight UIDs are eight prompt groups, not eight trajectory rows; global64 is the complete 8x8 diagnostic group.
Zero mean applies to the finite unweighted grouped row scores, not necessarily the token-weighted PPO loss or gradient when response lengths and microbatch denominators differ.

A failed zero-reward row in a group with positive mean receives a negative GRPO advantage; an all-constant finite group receives zero. This is relative outcome credit, not an oracle or proof of a correct gradient direction.
Comparing DT-PG with this official GRPO-PG is a same-data comparison, not a ground-truth bias measurement.

findings.claim: The actual trainer casts supplied DT Q/V/A tensors to FP32, verifies shape and finiteness, zeros masked entries, then supplies raw dt_token_advantages directly as advantages and dt_q_estimates as returns. It does not group-center or divide them by group std. The composer excludes zero-reward events and computes A=weighted_reward*(-expm1(-d)), V=weighted_reward*exp(-d), Q=sum(weighted_reward).
limits: A zero G event produces zero Q/V/A by the specified algebra; a zero sample is not itself proof of estimator bias.
A nonzero sample mean is not proof of statistical bias, and a finite or small advantage is not evidence of task quality.
The sum of saved row token_level_rewards is the owner row outcome used by GRPO; it must not be relabeled as every per-turn G_t or DT Q.
A=0 can also follow a zero log-ratio with nonzero reward; Q=0 can also include positions without mapped future-event support.

Preserve the accepted idealization that exact model-estimated values correspond to real-world variable values. Practical numerical or DT estimation error remains a separate possible issue, not a demonstrated cause here.

findings.claim: In the recorded static configuration, per-worker mini_batch_size32/micro_batch_size4 yields eight sequential B4 microbatches. Each PG/H/KL component is a masked token mean inside its B4, and the combined scalar is divided by eight before backward. Multi-turn actor loss uses the loss_mask response tail. For finite values, observation/padding mask-zero slots contribute neither numerator nor denominator. Zero-advantage policy slots remain in the mask denominator and the H/KL terms.
limits: A pooled global64 token mean is descriptive and is not the exact original PPO weighting unless all B4 mask denominators coincide.
The token fraction with A=0 can show sparse task support but cannot establish the strength or direction of the full task gradient.
Fixed H/KL coefficients with weaker task support can conditionally increase their relative influence; source/counts alone do not prove regularizer dominance or the observed decline.

findings.claim: The original FSDP2 group has gradient reduction enabled and passes its native mesh, dtypes and optional divide factor into foreach_reduce. The research observer measures the already-produced gradient shards. Its FP64 scalar SUM combines only sharded inner-product contributions; it does not introduce a second training gradient reducer.
limits: The installed _fsdp_collectives.py body is not among the locally saved sources audited here, so this receipt does not invent an additional numeric DP scaling factor.
Two rank gradient-statistics JSON results must not be summed again as independent full gradients.
Replicated/plain local-gradient ownership is not automatically treated as a sharded sum by the helper.

findings.claim: Actual low_var_kl/k3 uses d=ref_logprob-logprob, exp(d)-d-1, followed by clamp(-10,10). The actor computes a masked token mean of this sampled token matrix; the objective adds +kl_loss_coef times that mean. The logged actor/kl_loss is the coefficient-before mean.
limits: This is the sampled per-token estimator, not an evaluated full-vocabulary KL; the owner full KL branch is NotImplementedError.
The clamp caps finite extreme estimates, so a logged mean is not an uncapped distance summary. It does not remove NaN from non-finite intermediate arithmetic.
Logged KL near .117 cannot by itself show whether the reference model is correct or broken.

findings.claim: actor/kl_loss is assigned directly in every microbatch, so the returned scalar is the last microbatch of the last mini-batch/epoch on that worker. update_actor returns it inside DataProto.meta_info.metrics. Native DP collection concatenates DataProto outputs and uses only the first output meta_info. The trainer then calls reduce_metrics on that preserved metric dict.
limits: This source chain does not support calling logged KL a full-global64 mean or a cross-rank average.
The deprecated metric_utils wrapper delegates to verl.utils.metric; that implementation is not saved locally, and cannot recover metadata discarded by DataProto.concat.
Use first-collected-worker, rather than asserting a rank number not separately demonstrated by this receipt.

findings.claim: actor/entropy_loss in the original trainer is the unweighted entropy tensor from recomputed old-policy logprob, reduced over the original full batch response_mask before actor update. The actual helper prefers loss_mask. compute_log_prob runs the actor in eval mode under no_grad and uses recorded rollout temperature; entropy_from_logits uses natural-log logsumexp and softmax, yielding entropy in nats. Training entropy is a fresh train-mode forward inside each B4 and enters the objective with negative entropy_coeff.
limits: Logged H and logged KL differ in quantity, forward mode/timing and coverage. They are not a matched pair of full-minibatch loss components.

High late H (e.g.9.83) and modest logged KL (e.g..117) alone do not establish a damaged reference, a particular numerical failure, or regularizer-gradient dominance. These example numbers are parent-reported historical context and are not re-derived by this source audit.

findings.evidence_status: source-confirmed optimizer owner; update attribution unmeasured
findings.claim: The actual worker constructs AdamW with configured lr, betas and weight_decay; _optimizer_step first invokes the owner gradient clipping path and skips step if its returned norm is non-finite. Pre-clip gradient norms/cosines or a Gram-derived combined gradient are not a measured AdamW parameter update: adaptive optimizer state, coordinate-wise conditioning and weight decay affect the update.
limits: The isolated minibatch observer no-ops optimizer.step, so its results intentionally do not measure changed parameters or AdamW state evolution.
A combined norm/direction derived from component inner products must be labeled derived; it is not a separately executed combined backward pass.
Do not convert raw gradient dominance or alignment into an assertion about the actual AdamW update without recorded update evidence.

findings.claim: The saved v1 gradients are a real current-response B4 per worker from the loaded checkpoint, not a historical complete optimizer update. Their source references exactly match the actual actor/core/QVA identities above. The v4 entry receipt records original imports and configuration; a running collection is not a completed full-minibatch gradient result.
limits: A successful-response subset whose task norm exceeds H/KL does not settle dominance on the complete optimizer mini-batch.

This audit does not reconstruct unavailable historical35-40 full tensor batches or claim that the observed later decline has already been localized to task, entropy, KL, reference, dtype or optimizer.

The already-planned saved global batch and original component-gradient receipts can be analyzed with exact DP chunks and B4 mask denominators after completion; this is an interpretation boundary, not an extra launch, test gate, tolerance or method change.

plain_language_conclusion: 原PPO的防护仍在，但它们不保证给定优势的方向正确。若任务信号持续偏向错误方向，或相对固定的H/KL变弱，就可能每一步都有限、变化平滑，却逐步丢失任务能力。当前源码支持这些条件可能性，还没有把本次退化归因到某一项。G=0不等于理论有偏，GRPO不是oracle，普通梯度norm/cos也不是Adam真实更新。晚期高H与较低loggedKL的口径不同，不能据此判定ref损坏。
non_actions: No new optimizer, coefficient, scale, advantage normalization, learned value model or reward allocation proposed.
No SSH, GPU/model run, deployment, cleanup or commit performed by this audit.
